previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes was readmitted for persistent nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain shortly after an earlier discharge due to a family emergency. She had improved symptomatically at that time but experienced a recurrence of gastrointestinal symptoms, likely due to viral gastroenteritis exacerbated by premature advancement of diet. A CT scan showed no acute abdominal pathology, and labs ruled out diabetic ketoacidosis, though hyponatremia was noted and resolved with IV rehydration. A positive urine culture for E. coli was deemed contaminated due to lack of UTI symptoms and a normal repeat test. Her insulin was adjusted to a lower Lantus dose due to poor intake and hypoglycemia, with instructions to resume her regular dose at home. She gradually advanced to a regular diet, with nausea resolving, and was discharged in stable condition with follow-up recommendations.
